newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Coffee prices dive as Brazil warms up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Coffee prices dive as Brazil warms up.

text.p: Coffee prices fell sharply on Tuesday as weathermen forecast a warmer spell in Brazil, the world's leading producer.
Among other commodities platinum group metals began to ease from recent peaks as some traders saw an end to the extreme supply tightness.
London robusta coffee prices plunged $150 a tonne, wiping out early gains and taking the September futures price to $1,850, a $75 loss on the day.

Trade sources attributed the fall to a report by independent forecaster Weather Services Corp that the high pressure that brought cool weather to Brazil's coffee belt this week-end was heading out to sea and temperatures would be milder for the next few days.

June and July are key months in the coffee calendar when the Brazil crop is at risk to frost damage and short-terms speculators jump in and out of the market, depending on the latest weather forecast.

Precious metal traders noted an easing of recent tension in the very nervous platinum and palladium markets where the absence of 1997 shipments from major exporter, Russia, has drained the market of surplus supplies and sent prices soaring.
"Hopefully last Thursday and Friday was the peak of the panic,' a London based dealer said.
The reason for his optimism was comment from a Russian Finance Ministry spokesman that the state export agency Almazjuvelirexport should this week receive a licence for export.
This immediately brought some selling and profittaking into the market and prices for both metals fell sharply with platinum over $20 an ounce down at around $442.50 and palladium $17 lower at $208.
Major industrial metals like copper and aluminium both had a good day and continued to rally from last week's sell-off.

Copper traders warned of possible supply tightness during summer months if stocks continue to fall and the same situation could persist for aluminium if major producers continue to use stock to meet commitments rather than turn on idle potlines.
